title: Know if your idea sells. Before you build.
subtitle: One prompt that pressure-tests an idea in 5 minutes.

title: Most people build first, ask later.
subtitle: Six months building, then a launch to silence, then 'I guess the idea was bad.' The idea was fine. The order was wrong.

title: Validate before you write a line.
subtitle: Have AI play your skeptical customer and a market analyst before you burn a weekend on it.

title: The validation prompt
prompt: Act as a skeptical version of my target customer for this idea: [IDEA]. 1. What would make you NOT pay for this? 2. What do you use today instead, and what does it cost? 3. What would I have to prove for you to pay $20 a month? Then switch to market analyst: how many competitors exist, and where is the gap?

title: You're looking for one thing.
body: A specific, painful 'I already pay to solve this badly.' If the AI playing your customer shrugs, real customers will too.
tip: 4 to 12 competitors is the sweet spot: proven demand, room to win. Zero means no market. Fifty means too crowded.

title: The prompt is step one.
body: AI gives you the hypothesis. Then put up a one-page site, drive 200 people, and see if anyone pre-pays. A stranger paying before it exists is the only validation that never lies.

title: Run it on the idea in your notes.
subtitle: Paste the prompt, drop in the idea you've been sitting on, and find out today. Save it for your next one.
